# An attribute is a string, and a caller holding a number converts -- which is
# what html.sngl says three lines below the props that did not. `rows`, `width`
# and `height` were declared `int`, so the static render wrote the literal and
# the server render had nothing to write and aborted the build. Both paths on one
# program, so a divergence fails here rather than in one mode only.

sngl generate --lang go --platform html --out route route.sngl
grep 'rows=\\"4\\"' route/server.go
grep 'width=\\"100\\"' route/server.go
grep 'height=\\"50\\"' route/server.go

# The same program, same attributes, on the static path.
sngl generate --lang none --platform html --out static static.sngl
grep 'rows="4"' static/index.html
grep 'width="100"' static/index.html
grep 'height="50"' static/index.html

-- route.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:app"
import "sngl:platform/html"

output {
    go { html }
}

component main {
    var n string = ""
    window {
        textarea(:value=n, rows=4)
        html.img(src="a.png", width="100", height="50") {}
    }
}
-- static.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:app"
import "sngl:platform/html"

component main {
    var n string = ""
    window {
        textarea(:value=n, rows=4)
        html.img(src="a.png", width="100", height="50") {}
    }
}
